clean_source_blocks.text: Peru's presidential election is stuck in a statistical tie, according to an early tally by the pollster Ipsos, echoing previous elections that have dragged on for days or even weeks. It put the left-wing Roberto Sánchez on a marginal lead of 50.3% of the vote, compared with the right-wing Keiko Fujimori on 49.7%. While not an official count, the tally has been an accurate indicator of the final result in previous polls. Official results confirm the race is extremely tight with more than 85% of votes counted. The election pits Fujimori, a mainstay of Peruvian politics, against Sánchez, who is promising broad economic reforms. Concerns over crime and political instability have dominated the race. Recounts will likely be needed to confirm the winner, a process that could take weeks.
The race between right-wing Keiko Fujimori and left-wing Roberto Sánchez has been dominated by concerns over crime and political instability.

Three days out from Peru’s general election, voters are still waiting for results in the closely watched presidential race. Leftist candidate Roberto Sanchez moved into second place on Wednesday, as the vote count continues. But after years of political instability, Peru’s chaotic general election has done little to reassure voters that the tumult in their government is at an end. Peru has shifted through nine presidents in just 10 years. Then, on Sunday, the general election was marred by long lines and delayed ballot deliveries, prompting authorities to grant a one-day extension for voting in some areas. The confusion over the voting process and its results has spiked public scepticism. “We don’t know if the results are true,” Yeraldine Garrido, a 35-year-old receptionist in Lima, told the news service AFP.

Presidential candidate Keiko Fujimori of the Popular Force party greats supporters before heading to vote during the presidential runoff election in Lima, Peru, Sunday, June 7, 2026. Credit: AP/Martin Mejia LIMA, Peru — The winner of Peru’s presidential runoff election was not yet known hours after polls closed Sunday as electoral authorities slowly tallied votes cast for the ninth head of state in 10 years. Figures released by electoral authorities showed conservative politician Keiko Fujimori with a modest lead over nationalist congressman Roberto Sánchez with 58% of ballots tallied in a contest overshadowed by people’s concerns about surging crime. The outcome, expected to be tight, may not be known for days. The figures showed Fujimori received 5.96 million votes, or 52.6%, while Sánchez earned 5.36 million votes, or 47.4%.

original_article.research:
[Lähde: BBC World]
Peru's presidential election is stuck in a statistical tie, according to an early tally by the pollster Ipsos, echoing previous elections that have dragged on for days or even weeks.

It put the left-wing Roberto Sánchez on a marginal lead of 50.3% of the vote, compared with the right-wing Keiko Fujimori on 49.7%. While not an official count, the tally has been an accurate indicator of the final result in previous polls.

Official results confirm the race is extremely tight with more than 85% of votes counted.

The election pits Fujimori, a mainstay of Peruvian politics, against Sánchez, who is promising broad economic reforms. Concerns over crime and political instability have dominated the race.

Recounts will likely be needed to confirm the winner, a process that could take weeks.

Ipsos showed Fujimori dominating the capital Lima, carrying the urban vote and the coast, while Sánchez swept the rural vote and the mountainous Andes regions. Sánchez is expected to gain ground as ballots from rural areas are tallied.

Sánchez told supporters the early count was an "important lead that reaffirms the will of the people, who want democracy and justice."

Fujimori, on the other hand, said the result showed a "dead heat" and that there will be long "days ahead" to declare a winner.

She said it would be "irresponsible" to determine the result on early samples and that "every single tally sheet must be counted".

Sánchez also reiterated that he would seek a "presidential pardon" that would free the former left-wing president Pedro Castillo.

In 2021, Castillo also ran against Fujimori and finished with a similarly close result, which led to the declaration dragging on for weeks. Castillo was eventually jailed after trying to illegally disband Congress and govern by decree, and Sánchez served as a minister in his government.

Fujimori is one of the most well-known figures in Peruvian politics, and this is her fourth time running for office.

Her late father, Alberto Fujimori, was formerly the president of Peru and was eventually jailed for crimes against humanity. But his supporters credited him with a tough crackdown on violent insurgencies and implementation of social programmes to help some of the country's poorest.

His controversial legacy is one she leant into throughout the campaign, promising a tough military crackdown on organised crime, in particular extortion incidents that have soared in recent years.

Figures released by electoral authorities showed conservative politician Keiko Fujimori with a modest lead over nationalist congressman Roberto Sánchez with 58% of ballots tallied in a contest overshadowed by people’s concerns about surging crime. The outcome, expected to be tight, may not be known for days.

The figures showed Fujimori received 5.96 million votes, or 52.6%, while Sánchez earned 5.36 million votes, or 47.4%.

Electoral authorities took more than a month to declare them winners of that contest.

payload.title: Perun presidentinvaali on yhä äärimmäisen tiukka ääntenlaskennan jatkuessa
payload.summary: Perun presidentinvaalin tulos on jäänyt hyvin tiukaksi, kun oikeiston Keiko Fujimori ja vasemmiston Roberto Sánchez odottavat lopullisia ääntenlaskennan tuloksia.
payload.content:
Perun presidentinvaalin voittaja ei ollut vielä selvillä, kun ääntenlaskenta jatkui erittäin tasaisessa kilpailussa oikeiston Keiko Fujimorin ja vasemmiston Roberto Sánchezin välillä. Virallisten tulosten mukaan kisa on hyvin tiukka, ja yli 85 prosenttia äänistä on laskettu. Epävirallinen varhainen arvio asetti Sánchezin niukkaan 50,3 prosentin johtoon Fujimorin 49,7 prosenttia vastaan, mutta lopputuloksen vahvistaminen voi vaatia uudelleenlaskentoja ja kestää viikkoja.

## Ääntenlaskenta etenee hitaasti

Vaaliviranomaiset ovat laskeneet ääniä vaiheittain, ja eri laskentavaiheissa asetelma on ehtinyt näyttää erilaiselta. Aiemmin, kun 58 prosenttia äänistä oli laskettu, Fujimorilla kerrottiin olleen 5,96 miljoonaa ääntä eli 52,6 prosenttia. Sánchezilla oli tuolloin 5,36 miljoonaa ääntä eli 47,4 prosenttia.

Myöhemmät viralliset tiedot ja mielipidetutkimuslaitos Ipsosin varhainen arvio viittaavat kuitenkin siihen, että kilpailu on kaventunut käytännössä tilastolliseksi tasapeliksi. Ipsosin arvio ei ole virallinen tulos, mutta sitä on pidetty aiemmissa Perun vaaleissa hyvänä lopputuloksen ennakoijana.

## Rikollisuus ja epävakaus hallitsivat vaalia

Vaalikamppailua ovat hallinneet huoli rikollisuuden kasvusta ja maan pitkä poliittinen epävakaus. Peru on vaihtanut presidenttiä yhdeksän kertaa kymmenen vuoden aikana, ja nyt valittavasta johtajasta tulisi maan yhdeksäs valtionpäämies samalla ajanjaksolla.

Fujimori on pitkään Perun politiikassa vaikuttanut konservatiivinen poliitikko ja Popular Force -puolueen ehdokas. Sánchez on puolestaan vasemmistolainen ehdokas ja nationalistinen kongressiedustaja, joka on luvannut laajoja talousuudistuksia. Äänestyspäivää sunnuntaina varjostivat pitkät jonot ja viivästyneet vaalilippujen toimitukset, minkä vuoksi äänestystä jatkettiin joillakin alueilla päivällä.

## Lopullinen ratkaisu voi kestää

Epäselvyydet äänestysprosessissa ja tulosten odottaminen ovat lisänneet osan äänestäjistä epäluuloa. Limassa AFP:lle puhunut 35-vuotias vastaanottovirkailija Yeraldine Garrido kuvasi epävarmuutta sanomalla, ettei hän tiedä, ovatko tulokset totta.

Koska ero ehdokkaiden välillä on hyvin pieni, lopullinen ratkaisu voi riippua tarkistuslaskennoista ja siitä, miten jäljellä olevat äänet jakautuvat. Tiukka asetelma muistuttaa aiemmista Perun vaaleista, joiden vahvistuminen on venynyt päiviksi tai jopa viikoiksi.
summary_bullets: Perun presidentinvaalin tulos on yhä ratkaisematta ääntenlaskennan jatkuessa.
Roberto Sánchez ja Keiko Fujimori ovat erittäin tasaisessa kilpailussa.
Lopullisen tuloksen vahvistaminen voi vaatia uudelleenlaskentoja ja kestää viikkoja.

article.source_text:
Peru's presidential election is stuck in a statistical tie, according to an early tally by the pollster Ipsos, echoing previous elections that have dragged on for days or even weeks. It put the left-wing Roberto Sánchez on a marginal lead of 50.3% of the vote, compared with the right-wing Keiko Fujimori on 49.7%. While not an official count, the tally has been an accurate indicator of the final result in previous polls. Official results confirm the race is extremely tight with more than 85% of votes counted. The election pits Fujimori, a mainstay of Peruvian politics, against Sánchez, who is promising broad economic reforms. Concerns over crime and political instability have dominated the race. Recounts will likely be needed to confirm the winner, a process that could take weeks.

The race between right-wing Keiko Fujimori and left-wing Roberto Sánchez has been dominated by concerns over crime and political instability.

Three days out from Peru’s general election, voters are still waiting for results in the closely watched presidential race. Leftist candidate Roberto Sanchez moved into second place on Wednesday, as the vote count continues. But after years of political instability, Peru’s chaotic general election has done little to reassure voters that the tumult in their government is at an end. Peru has shifted through nine presidents in just 10 years. Then, on Sunday, the general election was marred by long lines and delayed ballot deliveries, prompting authorities to grant a one-day extension for voting in some areas. The confusion over the voting process and its results has spiked public scepticism. “We don’t know if the results are true,” Yeraldine Garrido, a 35-year-old receptionist in Lima, told the news service AFP.

Presidential candidate Keiko Fujimori of the Popular Force party greats supporters before heading to vote during the presidential runoff election in Lima, Peru, Sunday, June 7, 2026. Credit: AP/Martin Mejia LIMA, Peru — The winner of Peru’s presidential runoff election was not yet known hours after polls closed Sunday as electoral authorities slowly tallied votes cast for the ninth head of state in 10 years. Figures released by electoral authorities showed conservative politician Keiko Fujimori with a modest lead over nationalist congressman Roberto Sánchez with 58% of ballots tallied in a contest overshadowed by people’s concerns about surging crime. The outcome, expected to be tight, may not be known for days. The figures showed Fujimori received 5.96 million votes, or 52.6%, while Sánchez earned 5.36 million votes, or 47.4%.
